the use of 5 mm precision bore round quartz tubes for disc electrophoreses of proteins in polyacryl-amide gels and the use of a Gilford model-2000 spectrophotorimeter in a modified carriage for scanning the tubes directly at 280 nm provide a simple and rapid method for quantitation of the amount of any one protein in the gel.

the use of precision-bore quartz tubes for disc electrophoreses and direct scanning of the gels in an ultraviolet spectrophotometer permits the direct quantitative measurement of the amount of any protein in any peak of a gel.

the protein concentration of a solution can be determined by measuring its absorbance at 280 nm and that the absorbance at 260 nm of a solution can also be used to determine the protein concentration of the solution if the solution is not turbid.
